It continues to rise, reaching a peak of around 4,300 in 1964, marked by "1964 Surgeon General's report on smoking and health."

The line then fluctuates, with notable events and policies labeled along the way, including "Broadcast ad ban," "Nonsmokers' rights movement begins," "Federal cigarette tax doubles," "1986 Surgeon General's report on secondhand smoke," "Cigarette price drop," "FDA proposed rule," "2006 Surgeon General's report on secondhand smoke (an update)," "Federal $0.62 tax increase," "Family Smoking Prevention and Tobacco Control Act," "Master Settlement Agreement," "Nicotine medications available over-the-counter," and "Synar Amendment enacted."

The line eventually declines to around 1,000 by 2012. The y-axis is labeled "Per capita number of cigarettes smoked per year" and ranges from 0 to 5,000, while the x-axis displays the years from 1900 to 2012.
